forces.title: Ubiquitous DPI drives financial inclusion and digital participation.
forces.description: India's Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), exemplified by Aadhaar and UPI, has achieved massive scale, transforming financial services by democratizing access and driving digital participation nationwide. UPI alone processes over 18 billion transactions monthly, creating a rich real-time financial data ecosystem. This foundational infrastructure supports AI-driven underwriting, financial inclusion, and personalized banking, fostering a more connected and accessible economic system. Global adoption highlights DPI's role as a model for interoperable digital ecosystems and national competitiveness.

forces.title: Interoperable B2B digital rails streamlining commerce and credit.
forces.description: A significant structural shift is underway with the development of interoperable digital infrastructure for B2B commerce. This "canonical information exchange rail" aims to connect disparate business systems and banks, digitizing the entire order-to-cash cycle. By enabling standardized, real-time exchange of verified information (like invoices), it reduces manual reconciliation, improves transactional efficiency, and unlocks cash-flow based underwriting. This can transform MSME credit access and strengthen supply chain resilience, acting as a "B2B Operating System" that turns fragmented activity into a trusted, connected foundation for the nation’s next phase of growth.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: Agentic AI transforming finance from predictive to autonomous operations.
forces.description: Agentic AI is moving beyond simple automation to fundamentally reshape financial services, enabling autonomous decision-making across credit, liquidity, and compliance. This transformation is expected to make finance AI-native by 2030, with over 80% of operations influenced by AI agents, potentially reducing finance costs by 40-60%, shortening cash conversion cycles by 30-50%, and cutting decision-making time by 70-90%. This shift demands robust governance, transparency, and accountability frameworks to ensure responsible innovation and manage new AI-driven threat vectors like deepfakes and synthetic identities.

forces.title: RBI's unified master directions enhance tech and payment security.
forces.description: The RBI's issuance of consolidated Master Directions on Cybersecurity, Technology: Risk, Resilience and Assurance Framework, and Digital Payment Security Controls (July 2026) represents a significant structural shift in regulatory expectations for financial institutions. These directions establish a unified framework for technology governance, cybersecurity, operational resilience, and fraud prevention across regulated entities. Key changes include mandatory 6-hour cyber incident reporting, fixed VA/PT cadences, DR drill periodicity, and comprehensive coverage of third-party tech arrangements and digital payment product security for both financial and non-financial transactions, enhancing sector stability and trust.
forces.source_title: RBI’s technology focused master directions issued on 31 July 2026

forces.title: AI-generated fraud and cyber risks expand financial sector attack surface.
forces.description: The rapid advancement of AI significantly expands the cybersecurity attack surface for financial institutions. Generative AI enables attackers to create convincing phishing campaigns, automate vulnerability hunting, and conduct social engineering at scale, effectively bypassing traditional verification controls. Deepfakes and synthetic identities pose risks to KYC and account recovery, with regulators worldwide flagging these threats. This necessitates continuous, real-time intelligence sharing, robust governance frameworks for third-party AI, and significant investment in cyber resilience to combat evolving fraud patterns, data leakage concerns, and ensure business resilience at the board level.
forces.source_title: Beyond automation: How AI is reshaping the next decade of banking

forces.title: Stablecoins and digital assets driving new payment and market infrastructure.
forces.description: Stablecoins are emerging as a critical component of digital money infrastructure, supporting faster, lower-cost, and real-time value transfer. Financial institutions are increasingly exploring stablecoin-enabled networks to modernize cross-border payments, treasury operations, and settlement processes. This trend, coupled with the tokenization of financial assets, is reshaping next-generation capital markets by enabling greater efficiency, accessibility, and liquidity. Investment in digital asset infrastructure is growing, with corporate VCs actively participating to expand the ecosystem, despite lingering regulatory uncertainties, poised for substantial growth and innovation.

forces.title: India's push for sovereign AI and digital capabilities enhances resilience.
forces.description: India's strategic focus on building sovereign AI capabilities, alongside its robust Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), acts as a significant tailwind for the Fintech & Payments sector. Investments in AI infrastructure, talent, and innovation (e.g., BHASHINI platform, AIKosh, semiconductor investments) strengthen domestic technological competitiveness and reduce external dependencies. This ensures that critical financial services are resilient, secure, and accountable, fostering an environment for indigenous innovation and allowing India to potentially set a global benchmark for future financial operating systems by combining intelligence, trust, and scale at a national level.

forces.title: Rapid expansion of digital payments drives financial ecosystem growth.
forces.description: India has witnessed a rapid expansion in digital payment penetration, with the RBI Digital Payments Index significantly rising from 100 in March 2018 to ~517 by September 2025. This growth, driven by ubiquitous smartphone penetration and transformative public infrastructure like UPI, has made digital transactions a default mode of commerce nationwide. The high volume of UPI transactions (over 18 billion monthly) creates one of the world's richest real-time financial data ecosystems, laying a robust foundation for further AI-driven innovation in financial services, credit, and inclusion, contributing to broader structural transformation.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: Fintech consolidation intensifies, favoring scaled, proven business models.
forces.description: The global fintech market is experiencing intensified consolidation, particularly in the payments space, as investors concentrate capital on mature, scaled, and profitable businesses. While overall deal volumes are soft, deal values remain high, reflecting a preference for proven business models over early-stage speculative investments. Private equity investors are becoming more active in pursuing consolidation plays and roll-up opportunities for distressed companies that haven’t been able to attract investment or market share. This trend, driven by corporates seeking efficiency and growth, indicates a shift towards strategic acquisitions that accelerate capabilities and market position rather than broad, fragmented investments.

forces.title: Open credit networks to boost MSME credit access and data sharing.
forces.description: The Open Credit Enablement Network (OCEN) and Unified Lending Interface (ULI) represent significant upside drivers for digital lending, especially for MSMEs. OCEN, an open API network, connects lenders and digital platforms to deliver embedded credit. ULI, a consent-based interface, facilitates sharing of verified borrower data for faster and more accurate lending decisions. Combined with Account Aggregator, these initiatives make verified information portable and credit decisions more contextual, shifting underwriting from collateral to cash flow. This addresses the substantial MSME credit gap and enables transaction-based financing, improving financial inclusion and growth.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: Quantum readiness emerging critical for future financial security.
forces.description: Quantum readiness is becoming a critical strategic priority for safeguarding digital identities, payments, and financial infrastructure. As risks and complexity grow, firms are re-examining the long-term security of systems once considered immutable. This concern is prompting significant innovation and investment, with financial institutions, like Punjab National Bank, already implementing post-Quantum Cryptography for public-facing applications. The development of quantum-ready infrastructure is crucial to keep pace with financial services innovation and maintain trust in an increasingly complex digital environment, ensuring long-term resilience and security of financial systems.

forces.title: Government policies fostering AI innovation and financial inclusion.
forces.description: Strong policy support from the Indian government is driving innovation in AI-driven financial services. This includes regulatory innovation, institutional initiatives, and financial literacy programs designed to strengthen India's secure, inclusive, and technology-enabled financial ecosystem. Budget 2026 is expected to boost fintech, improve credit access, and reinforce financial inclusion. Such policy backing provides a conducive environment for the growth and adoption of AI across banking, payments, and lending, accelerating the transition towards an intelligent and future-ready financial operating system, and positioning India as a competitive, technology-driven financial hub.

forces.title: Manual B2B payment workflows create transactional inefficiencies.
forces.description: Despite rapid digital payment growth, B2B payment workflows largely remain manual and fragmented. This leads to process inefficiencies such as human-led onboarding, purchase order routing, invoicing, and payment execution, resulting in delays and errors. Disconnected systems and limited payment visibility slow collections and increase working capital pressure for MSMEs. This fragmentation means payment rails confirm money movement but not always its relation to specific invoices or deductions, hindering reconciliation and weakening working-capital visibility and control, posing a significant challenge to B2B commerce and MSME liquidity.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: Account Aggregator framework enabling consent-based financial data sharing.
forces.description: The Account Aggregator (AA) framework has enabled consent-based financial data sharing, evolving into a foundational pillar of India's digital financial infrastructure. With billions of consents fulfilled, AA facilitates secure and efficient exchange of verified borrower data, crucial for faster and more accurate lending decisions. This framework empowers consumers with control over their financial data, fosters interoperability, and supports the development of innovative, data-driven financial products and hyper-personalized banking experiences, contributing to broader financial inclusion. Its adoption is accelerating ecosystem-led innovation across financial services.
forces.source_title: Beyond automation: How AI is reshaping the next decade of banking

viewpoints.title: India poised to lead intelligent, sovereign, scalable financial operating systems.
viewpoints.description: KPMG in India asserts that India is uniquely positioned to lead the design of next-generation financial operating systems. This leadership stems from its unmatched combination of digital public infrastructure (DPI), technology talent, policy ambition, and market scale, notably exemplified by UPI and Aadhaar. The future of finance will converge AI, trusted data, programmable money, and DPI, transitioning from mere digitization to building intelligent, autonomous, and inclusive services at scale, setting a potential global benchmark for financial architecture that is intelligent, sovereign, scalable, and resilient by design.

viewpoints.title: Trust critical for AI-driven financial services amidst complex threat landscape.
viewpoints.description: Mastercard emphasizes that trust remains the ultimate differentiator in the evolving financial ecosystem. As AI progresses to agentic systems, innovation must be anchored by transparency, consent, accountability, and security, requiring trusted digital delegation where actions are traceable. Safeguarding the financial perimeter from complex, AI-driven threats necessitates continuous, real-time intelligence sharing and active collaboration among regulators, financial institutions, and technology leaders. This ensures that progress directly translates into economic inclusion for consumers and millions of MSMEs, underpinning India's growth engine and serving as a model for global digital transformation.

viewpoints.title: Fintech market momentum increasing, driven by AI and strategic consolidation.
viewpoints.description: Karim Haji of KPMG International sees a positive long-term outlook for the fintech sector. While current investment is concentrated on larger, high-quality deals, the broader market is gaining momentum. This is fueled by AI driving new opportunities, increased corporate activity, and private equity pursuing consolidation. Even smaller, differentiated startups are attracting attention, particularly in the digital assets, data management and analytics and core infrastructure spaces, suggesting a resurgence of investor confidence and a healthy pipeline of innovation despite geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainties.

viewpoints.title: Digital assets poised for growth, contingent on scaling infrastructure and regulatory clarity.
viewpoints.description: Anton Ruddenklau of KPMG International anticipates significant growth for major crypto firms, but this will largely depend on their ability to scale platforms and build resilient infrastructure. Regulatory clarity, such as the US's Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, is also a key factor. While early-stage investment is robust, particularly in digital assets, data management, and core infrastructure, addressing issues like interoperability and long-term quantum readiness will be crucial drivers for accelerated activity and innovation in the coming years, strengthening the foundation before activity accelerates quickly.

viewpoints.title: Interoperable B2B digital infrastructure crucial for India's next growth phase.
viewpoints.description: Shyam Unnikrishnan of Bain & Company and Dr. Noopur Chaturvedi of NPCI Bharat BillPay Limited argue that extending India's successful shared digital infrastructure model (like UPI) to the business economy is the next frontier. A trusted connective infrastructure for B2B transactions can reduce information asymmetry, strengthen supply chains, improve access to working capital, and support more informed commercial and credit decisions. This is framed as a national competitiveness agenda, promising to awaken and unleash India’s latent economic potential and drive higher productivity across enterprises of every size.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

viewpoints.title: Agentic commerce, sovereign capabilities to shape H2'26 fintech landscape.
viewpoints.description: KPMG's top predictions for H2'26 highlight agentic commerce as a key driver for investment in cybersecurity, digital identity, and payment infrastructure. Consolidation is expected to intensify in payments, with PE investors targeting distressed companies. Infrastructure for stablecoins and digital assets will become a major priority. AI investment will shift towards value-driven outcomes, favoring AI-native startups with defensible propositions. Lastly, the development of sovereign and regional solutions for digital identity management, cybersecurity, and other financial services infrastructure will gain prominence, building upon the positive momentum seen in H1'26.

viewpoints.title: Public sector banks integrate AI and CBDC for intelligent, sovereign, scalable finance.
viewpoints.description: Shri Ashok Chandra, MD & CEO of PNB, states that public sector banks are evolving beyond conventional banking to become integral parts of India's digital and economic infrastructure. PNB actively uses AI/ML for fraud detection, customer assistance, and employee learning, and has deployed a GenAI-powered assistant (PIHU) for real-time customer queries. The bank's participation in the CBDC ecosystem and implementation of post-Quantum Cryptography demonstrates a commitment to supporting national digital infrastructure and fostering secure innovation at scale for India's future-ready financial operating system.

viewpoints.title: Digitizing business information is next revolution for growth after payments.
viewpoints.description: Manasi Pandey, MD & Country Head, Global Payments Solutions at HSBC India, expresses a strong conviction that while India has successfully digitized the movement of money through platforms like UPI, the next significant revolution lies in digitizing business processes. She states that "When money, information and trust move together, businesses don’t just transact - they grow." This underscores the critical need for interconnected digital infrastructure beyond just payment rails to address B2B transactional inefficiencies and unlock India's latent economic potential by fostering greater collaboration and visibility across the business ecosystem.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

viewpoints.title: Unifying invoice-payment records essential for cleaner lending trails.
viewpoints.description: Vineet Sethi, Chief Growth and Marketing Officer at PayU, highlights the critical issue in B2B payments: invoices, payments, and accounting records often reside in disparate systems. He believes that once every payment is accurately linked to its corresponding invoice, a unified record and transaction history are created. This unified data provides lenders with a much cleaner and verifiable trail, significantly improving their ability to lend more confidently and efficiently, particularly to MSMEs who currently face credit access challenges due to fragmented information flows, ultimately fostering growth.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

viewpoints.title: Verified transaction data to transform MSME credit access.
viewpoints.description: Sunil Kamath, Group Head - Wholesale Banking Products at Axis Bank, asserts that the future of business financing hinges on transforming data into trust. As digital ecosystems become more interconnected, access to verified transaction and trade data can bridge the information gaps that have historically constrained credit access for MSMEs. He believes a neutral, interoperable infrastructure has the potential to strengthen underwriting, expand access to formal finance, unlock growth capital, and accelerate inclusive economic growth for this vital sector by shifting underwriting from collateral to cash flow.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit
